direct_answer: BASF integrates sustainability-related performance into incentives primarily through climate and other sustainability KPIs in variable remuneration for the Board of Executive Directors and senior executives. Specifically, reducing Group-wide CO2 emissions (Scope 1 and Scope 2) is anchored as the most important nonfinancial KPI in BASF’s steering and compensation systems and is one of three equally weighted strategic targets (33.3%) in the long-term incentive (LTI) for the Board of Executive Directors and senior executives [Source 1]. For senior executives in operating business units, BASF introduced a short-term incentive (STI) program with three additional (non-financial) targets alongside financial targets: occupational and process safety, sustainability, and development of the operating divisions; the first two are sustainability-related [Source 1]. These three objectives are equally weighted within the STI and together account for 25% of the total STI formula, meaning 16.7% of the entire STI formula is sustainability-related [Source 1]. The STI sustainability target includes elements contributing to BASF’s “green transformation,” such as sales of Sustainable-Future Solutions and increasing the share of purchased raw materials with supplier-specific Product Carbon Footprints [Source 1]. Supervisory Board remuneration has no variable components and is therefore not linked to sustainability target achievement [Source 1].
compliance_rationale: The passages provide key characteristics of the incentive schemes (LTI and STI), identify sustainability metrics/targets used (Scope 1&2 CO2 emissions; occupational/process safety; sustainability elements such as Sustainable-Future Solutions sales and supplier-specific PCFs), and quantify the proportion of variable remuneration linked to sustainability for LTI (33.3% of LTI) and STI (16.7% of total STI formula) [Source 1]. However, the evidence does not specify the governance level at which incentive scheme terms are approved and updated, nor does it fully describe assessment against specific sustainability-related impacts beyond the listed targets/metrics [Source 1].
disclosure_gaps: Level in the undertaking at which the terms of the incentive schemes/remuneration policies are approved and updated (for the Board LTI and senior executive STI) is not stated in the provided passages (ESRS 2 GOV-3(e)).

Whether performance is assessed against specific sustainability-related impacts (in addition to targets/metrics) is not clearly described beyond the named targets and example elements (ESRS 2 GOV-3(b)).

Confirmation of whether any sustainability-linked incentives exist (or do not exist) for other members of the administrative/management bodies beyond the Board of Executive Directors and the specified senior executive populations is not provided in the passages.
key_findings: Scope 1 and Scope 2 CO2 emissions reduction is the most important nonfinancial KPI in BASF’s steering and compensation systems and is embedded in variable pay [Source 1].
Board of Executive Directors and senior executives: CO2 reduction is one of three equally weighted strategic targets in the LTI (33.3% weight) [Source 1].

Senior executives in operating business units: STI includes sustainability-related targets (occupational/process safety and sustainability) within a 25% non-financial component; 16.7% of the total STI formula is sustainability-related [Source 1].

STI sustainability target includes, among other elements, sales of Sustainable-Future Solutions and increasing the share of purchased raw materials with supplier-specific Product Carbon Footprints [Source 1].
Supervisory Board remuneration has no variable components and is not linked to sustainability target achievement [Source 1].
